title: Answer a data-subject access request
summary: A DSAR looks like an ordinary email. It is a legal request with a statutory deadline. Under GDPR, respond without undue delay and within one month of receipt. You can extend two more months for complex or numerous requests, but only if you tell the requester within the first month (Art. 12(3), law rule eu.gdpr-dsar-response-deadline, EUR-Lex cited). The CCPA gives you 45 days, per the California AG's own page. Verify the requester's identity proportionately. Inventory everything you hold on them: product database, analytics, support desk, email tools, payment processor. Have counsel check the exemptions before anything goes out. An over-disclosure cannot be taken back, which is why sending is the irreversible step. Where the request is, or includes, deletion (GDPR Art. 17 erasure, CCPA request to delete), the same clock applies: execute the erasure across systems and processors, apply the statutory exceptions, and confirm what was deleted. Educational guidance, not legal advice; the controlling deadline is the statute's, verified at the primary source.

parts.title: Log the request and start the clock: one month under GDPR Art. 12(3), 45 days under CCPA — the extension needs notice inside month one

execution.rationale: Record the received request and counsel-confirmed statutory clock with its evidence in the case worksheet.

parts.title: Verify the requester's identity proportionately — enough to stop impersonation, never a data grab of its own

execution.rationale: Proportionate identity verification depends on the requester's relationship and the approved verification channel.

parts.title: Inventory where this person's data lives: product DB, analytics, support desk, email tools, payment processor

execution.rationale: Build a data-location map from the supplied system inventory and identifiers for the verified requester.

parts.title: Assemble the export and draft the response: what you hold, purposes, recipients, retention, sources

execution.rationale: Assemble supplied authorized extracts and draft the response with purposes, recipients, retention and sources identified.

parts.title: Review the exemptions with privacy counsel where it's close: third-party data, privilege, trade secrets

execution.rationale: Privacy counsel resolves close exemption and third-party disclosure questions against the actual response material.

parts.title: Deliver securely by the deadline and record what was sent (or send the extension notice inside month one)

execution.rationale: The verified requester's secure response or extension-notice channel is unspecified.

parts.title: Fix the intake: a records-of-processing map and a standing DSAR runbook so the next one is routine

execution.rationale: Draft the processing map and repeatable request-handling runbook from the reviewed case and actual system responsibilities.

parts.title: Execute the deletion where the request asks for erasure: delete or de-identify across your systems and processors, apply the statutory exceptions (GDPR Art. 17(3), CCPA §1798.105(d)), and record what was deleted and what was retained and why

execution.rationale: Erasure or de-identification requires each actual system and processor's supported controls and counsel-settled exceptions.

links.when: The request seeks access: a copy of the data and the processing details (a request to know).
The request is, or includes, deletion: a GDPR Art. 17 erasure request or a CCPA request to delete.

metadata.trigger: Someone exercises their data rights: a GDPR subject access request or CCPA request to know/delete lands in any inbox.
metadata.supportReason: The data inventory and the export assembly are agent work across your own systems; identity verification judgment, the exemptions review, and the decision to send are human, counsel's where it's close.

geoNotes.summary: UK GDPR's subject access request runs on the same one-month clock with the same two-month extension — the ICO's right-of-access guidance is the canonical employer-side playbook, including the identity-check and exemptions reality.

contextNeeded.query: the request itself and the date it was received (the clock runs from receipt)
